messages:
Sara: quick follow-up on the RFC we discussed yesterday — need a clear decision on where to do ‘region-cost cohorting’. do we bake cohorts at compile time (policy compiler) or do continuous scoring at runtime?

Kai: +1 to deciding. my gut: compile-time cohorts are simpler for low-latency fast-paths, but I worry about staleness and rollout complexity.

Miguel: agreed. data point from the perf bench: compiled cohorts cut decision CPU by ~40% and shaved ~0.8ms p99 on our microbench for short requests. runtime scorer gave better slot utilization (~6% more throughput) on spiky workloads.

Ada: tradeoffs spelled out:
- compiler/cohorting: deterministic, tiny decision latency, easier to cache, simpler telemetry attribution. harder to adapt to rapid regional capacity shifts and requires recompile/hotreload.
- runtime/scoring: adaptive, better short-term cost balancing, but heavier CPU and more state in the path (risk on cold paths). also complicates A/B and canarying unless we version scoring models.

Kai: important interface boundary question: if we keep cohorts in compiler we still need a tiny runtime check for compatibility (model variant, region blacklists). can we keep that check <0.2ms?

Sara: we measured a lightweight compatibility filter in the runtime at ~0.15ms median, ~0.5ms p99 for cold containers. warm p99 ~0.18ms. seems okay but adds another code surface.

Miguel: telemetry / observability asks: we need per-tenant cohort assignment histograms + exposed fallback counts. Also want a label that indicates whether a decision came from compiled cohort vs dynamic scorer — for regressions.

Ada: config proposal sketch (example):
```yaml
policy_engine:
  planner_mode: compiled # options: compiled | scoring
  compiled:
    cohort_ruleset: tenants/cohort-v4.json
    hotreload: true
  scoring:
    model: linear-lr-1
    weight_decay: 0.01
    cpu_budget_ms: 0.8
  runtime_checks:
    compatibility_timeout_ms: 1
    fallback_to_scoring: true
```

Sara: also thinking about migration: start with compiled cohorts for stable tenants, enable runtime scoring for a small percentage (~5%) of traffic as an experiment, monitor cost/loss metrics, then flip more. need an automatic fallback if scoring error rate increases.

Kai: implementation boundary: propose split of the policy repo into planner (compile-time artifacts + validation) and executor (runtime hooks + checks). executor exposes a slim interface: decide(request_meta) -> route_decision with provenance tag. planner produces artifacts and a small verification crate.

Miguel: +1. plumb provenance into route metadata: provenance=[compiled|scorer] and cohort_id. then Console can filter by provenance. also add a rolling mismatch alert when telemetry shows >1% divergence between compiled decision and a simulated scorer.

Ada: downsides: this split requires keeping the compiler and executor semver tight. hotreload surface must be robust (we already have a hotreload watcher but need to validate artifacts first or risk OOM on bad config).

Sara: ops question — how do we hotfix a bad cohort? can we push immediate runtime override?

Miguel: yes, add an override API that accepts a tenant->route mapping with high-precedence TTL. will be used only by SRE via Console. ops-bot should log overrides with audit trail.

ops-bot: override API deploy job queued by @Sara. build id: bld-4573, expected rollout 10:12 UTC, will log to /deploys/overrides.

Kai: decision proposal summary: 1) ship compiler-based cohorts as default for latency-sensitive routes, 2) keep runtime scoring as opt-in experiment (5% traffic), 3) split policy codebase into planner + executor, 4) add provenance telemetry and a mismatch alert, 5) provide an override API for fast hotfixes.

Ada: +1 from security/ops perspective, add auth check to override API and require 2FA.

Sara: sounds good. I'll draft an RFC addendum with the plan, small diagram, and timeline (prototype next week, canary in 2 weeks). assigning follow-ups: Kai -> executor interface PR, Miguel -> telemetry labels/alerting, Ada -> override API auth, Sara -> RFC addendum + canary plan.

Kai: I’ll open the executor PR today and include a tiny microbench for the compatibility check.

Miguel: will add simulated scorer run in the eval harness so we can compute divergence without impacting production.

Sara: thanks all. closing this thread, will ping when RFC addendum is up :thumbsup:
